displayName: Noe Valley corner shop (Victorian belt, ground-floor commercial)
_comment: #475. THIS TEMPLATE EXISTS BECAUSE OF A SCHEMA LIMIT, not because a corner shop wants its own
style. storefront_noe_corner is 5.55 m wide and owns the whole ground floor, so it cannot
share floor 0 with noe_valley_victorian's garage + door, and there is no 'exclusive with' or
'ground-floor slot' field to say so inside one template. Splitting into two templates that
both admit the belt is the expressible form: TryMatch collects every admitting template and
PickWeighted draws one per building, seeded by osm_id, so the split is deterministic and a
re-import is byte-stable. library.json's districtTemplateWeights sets the ratio (12:1).
The storefront carries its own recessed entry (entrySide/entryWidth/entryLeaves), so a shop
building needs no separate door part - which is why floor 0 holds exactly one exact here.
GATED BY NEIGHBORHOOD ONLY. It is not gated to commercial buildings, because it cannot be:
BuildingFactsJson.building_type is the raw OSM `building` tag and reads "yes" for 93.3% of
the 11,111 buildings measured in #472, so compatibility.building_types would either match
everything or nothing. Until #486 bakes a real commercial fact, roughly 1 in 13 buildings in
the Victorian belt - houses included - will be dressed as a shop. Do not add a building_types
filter here expecting it to help; it will silently do nothing.
Sizing is also not expressible yet: PlacePart applies uniform scale only and nothing carries
the real facade width into the part's `w`, so the 5.55 m shopfront is 5.55 m on a 4 m facade
and on a 20 m one alike (#487).
Windows start at floor 1: floor 0 is the shopfront.
The Mission and North Beach storefront/bay presets have no template yet - #492.
